title: From the Gibbs Weight to the Spectral Gap: A Complete Machine-Checked Osterwalder-Seiler Chain for the Z_2 Lattice Gauge Chain
abstract: A mass gap is a statement about the spectrum of an operator, whereas a lattice gauge theory is specified by a measure. This paper reports a complete formal verification in Lean 4 with mathlib of the Osterwalder-Seiler reconstruction passage for the Z_2 lattice gauge chain: from the Boltzmann weight exp(beta s) through reflection positivity, the Gelfand-Naimark-Segal space, the normalized transfer operator, and the identification theorem to the exact two-point correlation E_n[f(sigma_0)f(sigma_n)] = (tanh beta)^n, with verified non-vacuum eigenvalue tanh beta, spectral gap 1 - tanh beta > 0, and mass -log(tanh beta) > 0 for beta > 0. The underlying mathematics is textbook; the contribution is a machine-checked end-to-end composition proving that every interface composes without hidden assumptions. Limits are stated explicitly: one Z_2 variable per time slice (2x2 transfer operator, no spatial extent), fixed finite size (not volume-uniform), definite pairing (trivial GNS quotient), and no claim regarding SU(N), the continuum limit, or the Yang-Mills mass gap.
